newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids near midday Tuesday at $68.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $70.00, instances $71.00, as packers and owners continued their standoff, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of last week's sales were at $69.00, and several feedlot managers said they expected fed cattle this week to trade steady to firm on light supplies of market-ready cattle.
But cattle price strength this week could be blunted if beef prices keep retreating following recent gains linked to firm retail demand for pre-holiday and month-end promotions, sources said.

Memorial Day weekend, May 26, is generally considered the kickoff for the summer grilling season. Meat suitable for grilling, particularly ground beef, became the primary meat feature in retail advertisements early in May, a trend expected into August, the National Cattlemen's Beef Assn and Cattle-Fax Beef Featuring Analysis Program indicated.
Beef prices at midday were quoted by USDA down $0.14 to $0.67 per cwt on 209 fabricated loads sold.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted down $0.45 at $106.55, but down $1.93 since last Tuesday when prices started slipping, USDA statistics showed.
